text:
maya: idea for dedicated roadmap item: alpha a "transient burst buffer" for reserved pools. goal: give predictable short-term headroom with clear accounting + routing to best-effort capacity. want input on mechanics, billing, and launch checklist.

derek: high-level: is this different from graceband? sounds like a credit ledger that decays over time rather than a time window.

maya: exactly. propose per-tenant rolling credits (seconds of extra QPS) that accumulate modestly and decay. credits can be spent during microbursts. easier billing and reconciliation.

sara: pros: simpler billing and offline reconciliation. cons: harder to reason about latency SLOs if many tenants spend credits simultaneously. need global governors.

jon: routing question: when tenant uses credits do we keep serving on reserved pool nodes or spill to best-effort pool? I'd prefer prefer reserving reserved pool capacity first, then degrade to best-effort if global reserved headroom exceeded.

emily: commercial note: sales prefers an advertising story  "burst credits included" vs "surge billing". for pilots we can include small monthly bucket of free credits and bill overage at surge rates. billing team needs exact units.

billing-bot: recommended unit: credit = 1s * baseline_qps for tenant. bill per-credit at tiered rates: first N free in pilot, next at 0.4x, then 1.0x.

maya: proposed alpha config:
- credit accrual: 2s of baseline_qps per hour (caps at 120s)
- decay: credits age out after 24h if unused
- spend model: consume credits from oldest-first
- spill rule: if reserved pool global headroom < 10% then route to best-effort and mark as spillover

derek: infra notes: we can store ledger in a sharded timeseries store (one row/tenant) or Redis sorted set with expiry. prefer compact representation to avoid hot keys.

sara: perf guardrails: when serving credits on reserved nodes, attach a tenant_priority tag and enforce per-host hedging to avoid noisy neighbor effects. also add per-tenant concurrency cap when credits used.

jon: metrics required for launch:
- per-tenant credit_balance over time
- credit_spend_rate, credit_accrual_rate
- spillover_events and spill_latency_impact
- preemptions triggered while credit_active

emily: launch acceptance criteria proposals:
- pilot with 4 tenants total (mix of low + high QPS customers)
- no cross-tenant 99th percentile latency regression >15% for reserved pool tenants during pilot windows
- billing pipeline produces reconciliation CSV and matches pilot invoices for 95% of rows
- ops runbook completed and global headroom alerting in place

billing-bot: add requirement: exportable CSV schema: tenant_id, window_start, credits_accrued, credits_consumed, cost_usd.

maya: dev tasks:
- ledger service with API: accrue(), consume(), get_balance(), expire()
- router integration: consult ledger before allowing over-commit on reserved pool
- tagging: credit.earned, credit.spent, credit.spillover
- tracing: attach ledger_id to request traces for postmortem

derek: safety idea: emergency throttle "circuit breaker" that kicks in when more than X% of tenants simultaneously spending >Y credits. default conservative values.

sara: e2e tests:
- single-tenant microburst that fits in credits -> success, no spill
- sustained burst exhausting credits -> triggers spill/preempt path
- many tenants concurrent small bursts -> global cap enforces backpressure

emily: commercial pilot offer: include 30s credits/day free for 3 months during pilot. sales to prepare one-pager and FAQ. legal to review billing language.

maya: timeline suggestion:
- week 0-1: design doc + data model + billing schema
- week 2-3: proto ledger service + router hook in staging
- week 4: perf testing and chaos tests (concurrent spikes)
- week 5: pilot rollout behind feature flag to 4 tenants
- week 6-7: metrics collection and decision to iterate or GA

derek: questions on migration: when a tenant upgrades/downgrades committed quota do we adjust accrual proportionally? should be in design doc.

maya: yes adjust accrual rate on quota change and recalc cap. put in RFC.

sara: operational notes: retention of ledger events 30d for billing and 365d for audits (compressed aggregates). alert on discrepancy between ledger consumption and observed requests >1% for 24h.

emily: risks to surface:
- complexity in reconciliations and potential bill disputes
- platform oversubscription if we set accrual too high
- UI/UX clarity so customers know how credits behave

billing-bot: mitigation suggestions: explicit pilot contract clause, daily dashboard showing credit usage, dispute window 30d.

maya: next steps: I'll write RFC draft focusing on data model, accrual math, and spill routing. derek/sara to help with infra and perf experiments. emily to coordinate pilot marketing & contract language. I'll set a sync Thu to review RFC.

emily: I'll loop in finance and legal after RFC draft.

derek: I'll start spelunking Redis vs timeseries options tomorrow and post notes.

maya: thanks all. aiming for low-risk alpha that gives customers predictable short-term burst handling and clear billing.  :satellite:
